summary: Iteration 66 — Verified the RFQ parser Review Modal restructure end-to-end via a live Anthropic parse of /app/test_liner_rfq.txt on a fresh admin SA quote. Multi-part detection worked (2 components: Mid Disk 4 / Mid Disk 5). All 5 acceptance criteria from the review request PASS: (1) parse-mp-banner is rendered ABOVE parse-qty-verify in the DOM on both component tabs (compareDocumentPosition confirmed 'banner-BEFORE-qty'); (2) asks are strictly scope-filtered — Job tab shows only job-scope asks and HIDES the qty box, component tabs show only that component's asks with their scoped qty input; (3) parse-pricing-mode with Matched Set / Individual buttons appears ONLY on the Job tab and only because the parser was unsure (confidence 42% < 0.7, pricingMode null); (4) tab ask-count badges render on Job(6) and Mid Disk 5(3); (5) Apply Multi-Part succeeds — modal closes cleanly, quote loads with MULTI-PART · INDIVIDUAL pricing carried through, both components rendered with correct qtys and grand total $11,896.77, no console errors, no crash.

frontend: Login admin@standardprinting.com → fresh SA-260630-114401 draft loaded
Uploaded /app/test_liner_rfq.txt via files-browse-input (390 B, auto-classified RFQ)
Clicked btn-build-estimate → parse-review-modal opened in ~25s (cache hit 16,301 tok, M4 model, 42% confidence, $0.24 spend)

Job tab (default): parse-mp-banner PRESENT with parse-mp-tabs (parse-mp-tab-job[badge=6], parse-mp-tab-0=Mid Disk 4, parse-mp-tab-1=Mid Disk 5[badge=3]). parse-pricing-mode PRESENT with parse-pricing-matched-set & parse-pricing-individual (Individual auto-selected). parse-qty-verify HIDDEN. parse-asks rendered 5 job-scope cards only: parse-ask-job-outsideLiner, parse-ask-job-printMode, parse-ask-job-printSides, parse-ask-job-destZip, parse-ask-job-custCode — NO component asks leaked in

Clicked parse-mp-tab-0 (Mid Disk 4): parse-qty-verify APPEARED with parse-qty-input-item-0='2500'. DOM order verified via compareDocumentPosition → 'banner-BEFORE-qty'. parse-pricing-mode HIDDEN (correct — only shown on Job tab). parse-asks scoped strictly to Mid Disk 4: parse-ask-item-0-outsideLiner (1 ask). Header text: 'Fixes for Mid Disk 4 · 1 item'

Clicked parse-mp-tab-1 (Mid Disk 5): parse-qty-verify shows 'Verify quantities · Mid Disk 5' with parse-qty-input-item-1='2500'. Banner still above qty in DOM. parse-asks scoped: parse-ask-item-1-flute, parse-ask-item-1-boardGrade, parse-ask-item-1-outsideLiner (3 asks, matches badge). No item-0 asks bled in
Back to Job tab: confirmed parse-qty-verify still HIDDEN. Clicked parse-pricing-individual (already active). Filled parse-ask-input-job-destZip='44704'
Clicked parse-review-apply (labelled 'Apply Multi-Part (2 items)') → modal closed, no console errors, no error DOM nodes

Post-apply quote state: header shows 'Multi-Part · 2 / Mid Disk display components' with customer 'Acme Displays', Multi-Part INDIVIDUAL pricing header ('INDIVIDUAL · GM%'), 2 BOM rows (Mid Disk 4: 2500pc @$2.48, Mid Disk 5: 2500pc @$1.73), quote grand total $11,896.77 — Individual mode selection was honored end-to-end

critical_code_review_comments: FilesSec.jsx L952 (jobAskCount): counts include bare-string asks (a.norm==null) as job-scope which is correct behavior (the visibleAsks filter also routes bare notes under Job). Badge displayed 6 while 5 editable ask cards rendered — the delta is the non-editable custName ask that pairs with custCode. Cosmetically consistent; consider showing 5 to match rendered count, but current behavior is intentional per code comment.

FilesSec.jsx L637: pricingModeSel initial state uses p.pricingMode || 'Matched Set'. In this parse the parser returned Individual so the toggle mounted with Individual pre-selected. If a future parse returns null pricingMode with low confidence, the toggle would default to Matched Set — worth documenting for QA that the default is 'Matched Set' when the parser is unsure, not truly 'no selection'.

FilesSec.jsx L650 showQty condition (!isMP || mpTab !== 'job') hides qty box cleanly on Job tab. No regression on non-MP path — single quote still shows parse-qty-input-job (verified indirectly since this RFQ was multi-part; non-MP path is same code with isMP=false and no selector rendered).
The parse-mp-banner sticky header is nicely scoped, but on very small viewports the tab strip wraps into multiple lines with the pricing-mode block below — no overflow observed at 1920×1080.
seed_data_creation: Uploaded /app/test_liner_rfq.txt to fresh admin draft SA-260630-114401 (auto-created on login). Anthropic cache-hit, ~$0.24 spend on parser call 5 ($1.24 total / $500 cap). Applied quote created 2 BOM rows; quote left unsaved (draft state) — no cleanup required.
context_for_next_testing_agent: The Review Modal restructure is verified end-to-end. Key testids in the new order inside parse-review-modal body: parse-file-summary → parse-mp-banner (contains parse-mp-tabs with parse-mp-tab-job / parse-mp-tab-0 / parse-mp-tab-1) → parse-pricing-mode (Job tab only, when lowPricingConf) → parse-qty-verify (hidden on Job tab, shown per-component with parse-qty-input-item-{N}) → parse-asks (visibleAsks filtered to selected scope: parse-ask-job-{field} or parse-ask-item-{N}-{field}). The Anthropic parse for /app/test_liner_rfq.txt is cache-hit and returns confidence≈42% which reliably triggers the pricing-mode toggle. Note that after the first parse the .txt persists into Saved RFQ Files and Build Estimate flips to 'no RFQ file' on refresh — must re-upload the .txt to re-trigger runParse. Liner-label canonical round-trip (Kla-White → '42# Kla-White') was already verified in iteration_65 and the same AskEditor is used here; not re-tested because the modal was applied/closed after Apply verification.
rca of the issue: N/A — restructure works as designed. All acceptance criteria satisfied on the first live parse.
